newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cash crudes up on heating oil, arb, strike.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cash crudes up on heating oil, arb, strike.

text.p: U.S. cash crudes climbed on Wednesday morning, reflecting higher heating oil prices, the closed transatlantic arbitrage and concerns about an ongoing general strike in Colombia, traders said.
March West Texas Intermediate/Cushing was trading around $22.45-55 a barrel, up around 15 cents from late Tuesday's cash market.
The March/April WTI spread was around 32 cents.
Heating oil got a lift Wednesday from Tuesday's American Petroleum Institute (API) report indicating an unexpectedly large distillate stock draw.
The data, which reflects the week ended February 7, showed that distillate stocks, comprised of heating oil and diesel, fell 4.9 million barrels compared to expectations of a 2.5 million barrel drop.
Domestic grades were buoyed by the recently closed transatlantic arbitrage, which has prompted refiners to buy alternatives to North Sea barrels such as Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James.
LLS was around WTI/Cushing plus 36-40 cents a barrel, up up some 10 cents from late Tuesday. The grade moved at 35 cents.
WTI/Midland was at minus 36-34 cents, up three cents from Tuesday, with 38 cents getting done, traders said.
Heavy Louisiana Sweet/Empire was at parity with WTI/Cushing, up from the minus 20-10 cents on Tuesday.
West Texas Sour/Midland was alos up about five cents to minus $2.05-2.00 a barrel, with the grade changing hands at $2.00.
Eugene Island was minus $1.80-70 a barrel, up 30 cents from Tuesday. The grade was dealt at a discount of $1.80, traders said.
WTI/Cushing Posting Plus was steady around $2.00-03 a barrel.
